overview.overview:
Nebraska voted for the Republican presidential nominee by 19.05 points in 2020 and by 20.46 points in 2024. The forecast expects it to remain firmly Republican in 2028, with an expected Republican margin of about 15.5 points. The state leans roughly 20 points more Republican than the nation, and the plausible range runs from a Republican margin of about 6 points to one of about 25 points.

Recent statewide results point the same way. Republicans carried the 2026 Senate and governor contests by 5.9 and 7.7 points in the forecast's data. No state polls or home-state candidate information are available, so the outlook rests on past results and the statewide baseline. Nebraska's two electoral votes are unlikely to decide the national outcome.
overview.watch: A large shift in national opinion toward Democrats, or a major change in the state's political landscape, would be the most likely development to alter this outlook.
key_factors: Republican margins of about 19 to 20 points in the last two presidential elections
Republican leads in the 2026 statewide Senate and governor contests
No state polling currently available to test the baseline
